(c) NULL SEMANTICS — FINDABLE + CORRECT.
• Three-valued logic (TRUE / FALSE / UNKNOWN) LEADING CANONICAL at r23:1758-1801 (NOT IN + NULL gotcha): "SQL uses three-valued logic (TRUE / FALSE / UNKNOWN). When the right-hand subquery of NOT IN contains even a single NULL, every comparison outer_value NOT IN (..., NULL, ...) evaluates to UNKNOWN — never TRUE — so the WHERE clause filters out every row. This is standard SQL semantics, not a Trino bug; Postgres, MySQL, BigQuery, and Snowflake all behave the same way." + r23:2292 glossary entry.
• IS NULL / IS NOT NULL: ubiquitous — r23:442/1244/1271/1822/1856/1862/1911/1959/2247 (typed for explicit NULL-checks in WHERE; in NULL-fill ARG checks; in anti-join + IS NULL pattern). Two correct fixes given (Rewrite A: NOT EXISTS; Rewrite B: LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right IS NULL). Anti-join NULL-safety contrast at r23:1801 ("Unlike NOT IN, an anti-join is NULL-safe — NULL rows on the right side simply don't match anything, instead of poisoning the WHERE clause via three-valued logic").

ORDER BY ts DESC NULLS FIRST is the explicit form to preserve Oracle behavior; ORDER BY ts DESC NULLS LAST is the explicit Trino default.

=== DOCS-TRUTH (verified against trino.io/docs/467) ===
• JOIN semantics: INNER JOIN drops rows on no-match (both sides); LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched LEFT rows (NULL-fills right); RIGHT JOIN keeps unmatched RIGHT rows (NULL-fills left); FULL OUTER JOIN keeps both sides' unmatched (NULL-fills the missing side); CROSS JOIN = Cartesian product (no ON clause). OUTER keyword is optional.
• Join-key NULL never matches: standard 3VL — NULL = NULL evaluates to NULL/UNKNOWN, so the equi-join predicate fails and the row does NOT match (NULL does NOT join to NULL). Use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM for the NULL-safe equi-join (treats NULL = NULL as TRUE).
• Fan-out / row-multiplication: when joining ONE parent row to MANY child rows on a key that has duplicates on the child side, the parent row is duplicated once per matching child → SUM(parent.metric) is INFLATED by the multiplier. Fix: pre-aggregate the child to ONE row per join key in a CTE FIRST, then join the pre-aggregated CTE to the parent. (Or use SELECT DISTINCT on the child for non-aggregate joins.)
• Correlated subquery = the inner query references a column from the outer query (each outer row may yield a different inner result). Uncorrelated = inner query is self-contained and runs once.
• EXISTS / NOT EXISTS: returns TRUE/FALSE per outer row (never UNKNOWN). NULL-safe (NULLs on the right are simply ignored).
• Scalar subquery: returns exactly ONE value; if it returns >1 row, Trino raises an error at runtime ("Scalar sub-query has returned multiple rows"); if it returns 0 rows, returns NULL.
• WITH RECURSIVE: SUPPORTED in Trino 467 (since Trino 340, 8 Aug 2020). Required shape: WITH RECURSIVE t(cols) AS (base_query UNION recursive_step) SELECT * FROM t. The RECURSIVE keyword IS required. UNION (the docs say "shaped as a UNION of two relations" — both UNION and UNION ALL work for the join; UNION ALL is typical). Default max_recursion_depth = 10 (session-tunable). Plan-growth is quadratic with recursion depth (docs verbatim). Flagged as experimental in docs.
• Three-valued logic: NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN (not TRUE). NULL <> NULL also evaluates to UNKNOWN. WHERE clause filters out UNKNOWN. To check for NULL, use IS NULL / IS NOT NULL operators.
• NOT IN + NULL trap: NOT IN (subquery-with-NULLs) returns ZERO rows (every comparison evaluates to UNKNOWN; the WHERE filters all). Fix: NOT EXISTS (NULL-safe) or LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right IS NULL (anti-join). Both decorrelate to SemiJoin in EXPLAIN.
• NULLS ordering default: Trino docs verbatim — "The default null ordering is NULLS LAST, regardless of the ordering direction". Both ORDER BY x ASC and ORDER BY x DESC default to NULLS LAST. (This DIFFERS from Oracle, which defaults to NULLS LAST for ASC + NULLS FIRST for DESC.) Always write the explicit NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST when migrating Oracle SQL.
• date_parse(str, fmt): MySQL format specifiers (%Y %m %d %H %i %s); returns timestamp(3) WITHOUT zone.
• parse_datetime(str, fmt): Joda format (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss); returns timestamp with time zone.
• CAST(str AS TIMESTAMP): only for raw ISO-8601 string (`2026-05-30 12:00:00` or `2026-05-30T12:00:00`). No format string accepted.
• from_iso8601_timestamp(str): for ISO-8601 string with optional zone offset (returns timestamp with time zone). from_iso8601_date(str): for ISO-8601 date string (returns DATE).
• parse_date / TO_DATE / STR_TO_DATE: NOT Trino functions. Use the four functions above.
